Several GPS localization methods are used frequently in road networks in the modern era, including Differential GPS (DGPS), Dead Reckoning, Sensor Fusion, Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) GPS, and map-matching. The technique that is used is determined by the application needs, such as precision, dependability, and availability of GPS signals, as well as by the infrastructure and financial constraints that are in place. This paper offers an evaluation of various GPS localization methods that are frequently utilised in road networks along with some of the challenges faced in using these techniques.

articleTitle: Progression Study on Privacy-Preserving Big Data Publishing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Informatics (IC3I)
abstract: In today's virtual world, it is vital to preserving privacy wherein the information is amassed from different sources with sensitive information at an exceptional level had been the benefits may be gained from the big data by publishing the data for research without jeopardizing the privacy of an individual personality. Traditional anonymization techniques have been used to protect personal information of individuals for research or market decision-making purposes. However, these techniques are not suitable for Big Data due to its large volume, high velocity, and variety of data. Advanced techniques are necessary when working with Big Data because traditional techniques cannot handle the storage and analysis of large amounts of data. The aim of this paper is to ensure privacy in Big Data by conducting a comparative study of various techniques.

articleTitle: Enhanced Method of Detection of Skin Defects in Citrus Fruits Using Convolutional Neural Network Algorithm in Comparison with Principal Component Analysis Method to Improve Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Informatics (IC3I)
abstract: Aim: To identify key characteristics and evaluate accuracy of identifying skin diseases in citrus fruits on their surface using a novel convolutional neural network compared with principal component analysis. Materials and method: To investigate the accuracy for the dataset containing sample size (N=10), two techniques namely a Novel Convolutional Neural Network algorithm and Principal Component Analysis algorithm were incorporated with G-power=0.8. Result: It was discovered that the categorization accuracy of CNN was found to be (91.82%) whilst the principal component analysis algorithm's accuracy was (62%) using citrus diseases dataset. The T-test shows that the convolutional neural network classifiers appear to be of superior significance than principal component analysis with p=0.03 (p<0.05). Conclusion: In this article, types of citrus diseases are classified using the two models, PCA and CNN. The models helped in extracting discriminative characteristics from the input images. From results, it can be concluded that in comparison to other methodologies, the deep learning methodology is a pragmatic approach.

articleTitle: Handwritten Digit Recognition Using CNN with Average Pooling and Global Average Pooling
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Informatics (IC3I)
abstract: Recognition of handwritten digits is crucial because it enables computers to comprehend and understand human handwriting. The automatic sorting of mail, processing of financial records, and reading of prescriptions are only a few examples of its many practical uses. It can also be used in the classroom for exam grading. The automating process with handwritten digit recognition eliminates mistakes and saves time. The major goal of this paper is to examine several existing model configurations and give trustworthy and effective ways for detecting transcribed numerical data. This paper highlights Convolutional Neural Network (CCN) with Average Pooling (AP) and Global Average Pooling (GAP) layer for proper extraction of insights from the feature maps. Results indicate that the proposed Convolutional Neural Network classifier with AP and GAP layer outperformed existing neural network with significantly increased computational efficiency without sacrificing execution. This paper development is based on the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology, or MNIST dataset, which is a well-known handwritten digits dataset in the machine learning and computer vision fields. Each handwritten digit is a 28x28 grayscale image, and there are 70,000 of them in total numbers from 0 to 9. Thus, the classification model is of classes 10. 60,000 images are there in the training dataset and 10,000 images are there in the testing dataset. The proposed CNN Model with AP and GAP Layer achieves a classification accuracy of 99% on the MNIST Dataset.

articleTitle: Spam Detection Using Machine Learning Algorithms and AdaBoost Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Informatics (IC3I)
abstract: - E-mail has become an integral part of every individual's life. All sorts of communication formal and informal are carried out through this channel. As it is relatively cheaper and reliable, it has recently become a target for marketing agencies and hackers. A large number of unsolicited emails, called spam, containing either malicious content or unwanted advertisements, are sent to the individuals on a daily basis. This makes it difficult for e-mail service providers to segregate spam from non-spam (ham) e-mails. Consequently, important e-mails are often lost in spam, causing losses consumers and wasting valuable resources. The trust of consumers is compromised when their private information is accessed. This is where the need for improved performance of machine learning classifiers is felt. The aim of this paper is to classify spam emails by using supervised machine learning classifiers with and without Adaptive Boosting, and to conduct a deep analysis by using performance metrics. A significant improvement in the accuracy of SVM and Decision Tree has been observed.

articleTitle: Dynamic Path Allocation Based on Reinforcement Learning in Iot Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Informatics (IC3I)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) expands Internet accessibility to billions of IoT devices around the world, where the devices collect and provide data to represent the actual state of the world. On the other hand, over a long period of time, the Independent Control Framework (ACS) carries out control functions on the actual systems without external interference. articleTitle: Real Time Image Placement Using Augmented Reality on Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Informatics (IC3I)
abstract: Home decoration is the art of enhancing the aesthetic appeal of a living space. One of the key elements of house décor is picture wall decor. People adore hanging up memories-inspired pictures on their walls. The conventional approach is to visualise the arrangement, frames, and photos before hanging them up. In this paper, different methods have been suggested incorporates augmented reality to change the traditional method. Using this approach anyone can scan the walls using smart phones and place the images on the walls. The wall detection methods that are now available do not offer a very good experience in wall detection and picture positioning. Although high-end devices produce superior results, the objective of this paper is to improve the user experience for devices in the middle of the spectrum. The experiments demonstrates the development of augmented reality applications that can run on low-end ARCore-compatible devices and deliver performance on par with high-end ones.
